project_scope.note: This is the initial Papaveraceae family file for Hays Botany ID. Future Papaveraceae genera should be merged into this file rather than replacing it from scratch.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: For local Argemone, inspect the flower base and developing capsule: quickly falling sepals, free petals, many free stamens, superior ovary and prickly capsule. Latex is supporting evidence, not a reason to injure a plant.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate, exstipulate and commonly lobed/divided; local prickly poppies are strongly armed and glaucous.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Radial; 2–3 sepals commonly caducous; petals free; stamens numerous and free.
family_diagnostics.ovary: Superior and syncarpous; local Argemone develops a prickly capsule with many seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Family-wide identification: compare bud sepals, stamens and mature capsule. Argemone is prickly with many free stamens, but Corydalis has a spurred bilateral flower and six stamens in two bundles; Eschscholzia sheds a fused sepal cap and Papaver often has a stigmatic disc above capsule pores. Do not define all Papaveraceae by prickles or radial flowers.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → diagnostic structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Prickly poppies are a great lesson in ignoring petal color and looking at sepals, free stamens and the capsule.

steps.title: 1 · Recognize the armed habit
steps.look_for: Glaucous, prickly lobed leaves and armed stems.
steps.why_it_matters: Gets you to Argemone quickly before fruiting.

steps.title: 2 · Watch the sepals disappear
steps.look_for: Horned sepals on the bud that fall as the flower opens.
steps.why_it_matters: Caducous 2–3 sepals are a strong Papaveraceae clue.

steps.title: 3 · Count the free stamens
steps.look_for: Numerous free stamens surrounding a syncarpous central ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates the poppy pattern from Malvaceae's fused staminal column.

steps.title: 4 · Read the capsule prickles
steps.look_for: Very unequal long prickles, commonly branched in A. aurantiaca.
steps.why_it_matters: Capsule armature is a much stronger local species character than petal color.

steps.title: 5 · Compare the other prickly poppy
steps.look_for: Shorter/simpler fruit-prickle architecture relative to A. aurantiaca.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the high-value local two-species comparison.

comparisons.title: Papaveraceae vs Malvaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have many stamens. Papaveraceae keeps them mostly free around a capsule-forming ovary; local Malvoideae commonly fuses stamens into a staminal column.

visual_lesson.caveat: Observe latex only from existing damage when possible; do not injure plants solely for a field test.
